Filed as I-0623. Review complete.

## Verdict

The mathematics is sound and the Lean is real. One scope claim is materially wrong, and it is the provenance claim — not any of the three you flagged as most likely.

**The central claim holds.** The H1 peel genuinely is a theorem on the chi-ledger carrier. `surjective_hModule_one_divisorSheafLE` (SectionDrop.lean:151) is two lines off `Sheaf.HModule.surjective_map_f` (ChiSlice.lean:112) with `Subsingleton (H¹ sky)` from `skyModule_subsingleton_hModule_one`. No hidden hypothesis.

**Your six questions, answered.**

1. **No trap (d).** `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le` proves what it says. Its binder block (SectionDrop.lean:102-106) is *byte-identical* to ChiLedger.lean:65-69 — `diff` is empty — and `ChiCurve.chi_divisorSheaf_curve` already elaborates against exactly that block at the challenge curve, discharging both `Module.Finite` binders. Instantiability is inherited, not assumed. Your own probe `scripts/ajcrr-sectiondrop-axioms.lean` however **cannot elaborate right now**: Lean returns "Imports are out of date" because `Ledger/Basic.lean` is newer than `ChiCurve.olean`. Its `#print axioms` lines currently assert nothing. `SectionDrop.olean` did land at 21:42 and is fresh against source.

2. **Counts correct, no leak.** 19 declarations, 11 `omit` lines, verified against disk. The conclusion holds too: `divisorSheaf` (DivisorSheaf.lean:326), `devissageSES_shortExact` (DevissageExact.lean:316), and the Devissage variable blocks carry no `Module.Finite` binder at all, so no finiteness can enter through them. The `Subsingleton`-over-`finrank` reasoning also checks out — `Sheaf.h1` is `Module.finrank` (Chi.lean:86), which reads 0 on infinite-dimensional modules.

3. **The scope caveats are honest, and better than when you wrote the task.** Both reductions are labelled as reductions at the declaration. The order-cone / degree-half-space distinction is stated consistently at the module docstring, at `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le`, at `h0_divisorSheaf_of_subsingleton_of_le`, and in the `DegreeThreshold` section note. Your two later commits (4d034feb0, 93fdd8608) caught the dangling `h0_sub_h0_sub_point_lt` and narrowed the adelic claim before I got there.

4. **Accurate.** `coneVanishing_iff_base_and_peel` (BoundedVanishing.lean:604) is a real `↔`; the forward direction takes `y = 0`. So on the adelic carrier base+peel is equivalent to cone-vanishing. Your later self-correction is the right one though: `LedgerClosure.peel_pointDivisor_of_notMem_overlap` (:441) does discharge the peel off the overlap, so "wholly open" would have been too strong.

5. **This is the wrong claim.** "AJCR has the h1 INEQUALITY; it does not have the vanishing propagation" is false. AJCR has the propagation in `Subsingleton` form as a complete chain, already finiteness-free:

   `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/FLVClass.lean` — `peel_single`:260, `peel_nsmul_single`:277, `peel_effective`:292

   `peel_effective` matches your `subsingleton_hModule_one_add_effective` statement-for-statement up to the name, same `(A E : X.CurveDivisor) (hE : 0 ≤ E)`, and the FLVClass Peel variable block (:253-257) omits both `Module.Finite` instances. The bodies share locals `b, E', hdecomp, hcard, hsingle, hsplit, hne, hp, hEF` in the same order with the same lemma choices, differing only at the concluding line. "ADAPTS" understates it, and you cited the wrong ancestor: the finrank lemma, not the Subsingleton twin. "Run on Subsingleton instead of finrank, which is what removes the finiteness" describes work AJCR had already done. `h1_le_h1_sub_point` is also a duplicate of AJCR `SectionBound.lean:67 h1_le_h1_sub_single`. Your own `Adelic/BoundedVanishing.lean:83-96` already names `FLVClass.peel_effective` — the name was reachable from inside AJC.

   Genuinely new and absent from AJCR, confirmed by search: `h0_sub_point_le` (AJCR never uses `finrank_le_finrank_of_injective`), the two-sided drop (`residueDeg` never co-occurs with `Sheaf.h0` in AJCR), the ℤ-valued drop identity, the order-cone form `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_le` (AJCR only ever does degree-threshold plus class transport), and the exact-RR/cofinality layer.

6. **No collisions.** All 19 names are unique within AJC and absent from Mathlib.

7. **Scope clean.** Each of the three commits touches only `SectionDrop.lean` against its own parent (one `A`, two `M`), no deletions, no foreign paths, nothing in `WeilDivisor.lean`, `Picard/**`, `Cohomology/**`, or the root roll-up.

**Two smaller defects.** The "What is proved" list cites `h0_divisorSheaf_le_of_le` and `h1_divisorSheaf_le_of_le` (SectionDrop.lean:26) — neither exists anywhere in the project; the real names are `h0_sub_point_le` and `h1_le_h1_sub_point`. Same class as the `h0_sub_h0_sub_point_lt` dangler you already fixed. And `moduleFinite_devissage_X₃_zero` (:123) is dead — private, never referenced.

**Navigability.** The whole 42-file `Ledger/` tree is still unrooted: nothing outside `Ledger/` imports it except `WeilDivisor.lean` pulling in `OrdCompare` and `ResidueOneAlgClosed`. `SectionDrop` reaches no library root, so the workspace axiom probe does not cover it. That is I-0600, already open.

**Highest-value next action.** Correct the provenance note and the team-thread headline to say the peel chain re-derives `FLVClass.peel_effective` rather than supplying something AJCR lacks, and narrow the claimed novelty to the order-cone form, the drop identity, the two-sided drop, and the exact-RR/cofinality layer. Filed as **I-0623** with the search rule that would have caught it: grep the target *conclusion type* across siblings (`Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule _ 1)` as both hypothesis and conclusion), not the proof technique you expect to use. The two dangling docstring names are a one-line fix to make alongside it.
